REAL FINDING (the reason this iteration exists): the test was CONFOUNDED -- 'fixed' mode is read by BOTH the pre-TP1 arm branch AND the post-TP1 runner branch (TP1 fill unconditionally sets profit_lock_armed=True + resets runner_stop=entry regardless of arm_pct/arm_scope), so selecting profit_lock_mode='fixed' silently DISABLES the post-TP1 15%-trailing chandelier for any trade that reaches TP1. At arm=0.50 only 2 of 27 degraded trades were the pre-TP1 whipsaw the hypothesis targeted; 25 of 27 (-$3,226) were post-TP1 loss-of-trailing-protection. The pre-TP1-floor-only hypothesis has therefore NEVER been cleanly tested -- the pre-existing ExitShape vocabulary could not express it.

what_iterations_1_2_3_established.conclusion_carried_forward: A TRAILING lock (floor = HWM*(1-trail_pct)) clips runners on premium PULLBACK, which on 0DTE is often theta bleed, not reversal -- iterations 1-2 established this cleanly (profit_lock_mode held 'trailing' throughout, so their runner-cohort damage came ENTIRELY from pre-TP1 whipsaw). Iteration 3 could not isolate a pure BE-floor pre-TP1 test because 'fixed' mode is a shared knob across both branches. THIS iteration adds a NEW, structurally independent knob (pre_tp1_be_floor_arm_pct on exit_manager.ExitState/plan_exit_actions, shipped this same fire, see backtest/tests + automation/state/fleet/test_exit_manager.py's new ISOLATED PRE-TP1 BE FLOOR test block) that arms a BE-floor-ONLY scratch pre-TP1 while profit_lock_mode STAYS 'trailing' throughout -- so the post-TP1 chandelier (the +$15,774.05/35-for-35 runner engine) is PROVABLY untouched (TP1 fill unconditionally re-arms profit_lock_armed=True and resets runner_stop=entry regardless of this knob; guard test test_pre_tp1_isolated_floor_post_tp1_trailing_byte_identical_to_control pins this).

hypothesis: Arming a BE-floor-ONLY scratch pre-TP1 (never ratchets past entry, never trails pre-TP1) via the NEW pre_tp1_be_floor_arm_pct knob converts round-trip-to-loss trades (yesterday's 2026-07-28 shape) into scratches, WITHOUT touching post-TP1 trailing protection for any trade that reaches TP1 -- unlike iteration 3's confounded 'fixed' mode. PREDICTION TO BEAT (named in the queue item before this run): if the pre-TP1 whipsaw really is only ~2/27 of iteration 3's damage at a high arm threshold, an isolated pre-TP1-only floor at arm_pct=0.50 should be roughly NEUTRAL-to-positive on the runner cohort while still converting round-trips into scratches. If it fails too, the exit leak is not addressable via any profit-lock mechanism on this axis and the axis CLOSES for good -- move to the THETA-NOT-GIVEBACK hold-time/underlying-stall class instead (queue.md, filed alongside this item).
mechanism_new_this_iteration: pre_tp1_be_floor_arm_pct is a NEW field on exit_manager.ExitState (default None = fully inert, byte-identical to every pre-existing persisted record and every pre-existing ExitShape). When set, plan_exit_actions arms a BE floor (runner_stop = max(runner_stop, entry)) the first tick best_premium clears entry*(1+pre_tp1_be_floor_arm_pct) -- and NEVER ratchets it further pre-TP1 (no trailing pre-TP1, regardless of profit_lock_mode). Critically, it does NOT set profit_lock_armed=True, so it cannot interact with the post-TP1 arm-level check at all; post-TP1 is governed purely by profit_lock_mode (kept 'trailing' in every candidate cell below), and TP1 fill's own unconditional profit_lock_armed=True/runner_stop=entry reset (exit_manager.py line ~456-457) means post-TP1 state is IDENTICAL regardless of this knob's value. This is the structural fix to iteration 3's confound, not a re-run of the same test.
